library(tidyverse)

# Background

Your Cuban uncle sets up a cocktail bar in downtown Budapest. He has a secret list of cocktails that he would like to serve in the bar. He asks you to do create a few lists and tables to set up the shop. As your uncle is a secret hipster, he has a dataset on Github that you can use for the task!

![](https://media1.tenor.com/images/57a519cffd0ad4693be3b9c94b211540/tenor.gif?itemid=5195211){width="320"}

Note: There are several different ways to solve these tasks, feel free to come up with your own.

## 1. Read the data

Read the cocktail dataset from: <https://github.com/nthun/cocktail-balance> You can also find the codebook there.

```{r}

url <-  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nthun/cocktail-balance/master/cocktail_data.tsv"
cocktail_data <- read_tsv(url)

```

## 2. Transform the data table and clean the ingredient variable!

The ingredients are currently in a single cell for each cocktail. It would be better to put them in separate rows. Also, the variable should be cleaned of all quantities (e.g. 1/2 oz, 2 dashes, etc.), and the indicator of alcohol content (e.g. 47.3% abv). You will need to use this cleaned table in later tasks.

```{r}
ingredients <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(name, ingredients) %>%
    separate_longer_delim(cols = ingredients, delim = "<br/>") %>%
    mutate(ingredients = str_remove(ingredients, " oz")) %>%
        mutate(ingredients = str_remove_all(ingredients, " oz|% abv|1/2|3/4|1/4|[0-9]+|\\(|\\)|/| bsp")) %>%
        mutate(ingredients = str_remove_all(ingredients, "drops|drop")) %>%
        mutate(ingredients = str_remove_all(ingredients, "dashes|dash")) %>%
        mutate(ingredients = str_squish(ingredients)) %>%
    mutate(col_name = paste0("ingredient_", row_number()), .by = name) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = col_name, values_from = ingredients)

cocktail_data <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(-ingredients) %>%
  left_join(ingredients, by = "name")
  


print(head(cocktail_data))
```

## 3. All ingredients in alphabetical order

Before opening the bar, you need to find a reliable supplier that has all the ingredients. 
You need to send a list of all possible ingredients you will need. 
They don't need the quantities (i.e. how many of these are needed), just the names of the ingredients.

```{r}
all_ingredients <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(starts_with("ingredient_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("ingredient_"), values_to = "ingredients") %>%
  drop_na(ingredients) %>%
  distinct(ingredients) %>%
  arrange(ingredients) %>%
  pull(ingredients)

all_ingredients
```

## 4. Number of unique ingredients

How many different ingredients you will need?

```{r}
#The number of unique ingrredients:
length(all_ingredients)

```

## 5. What are the top 10 ingredients?

What are the 10 most frequently used ingredients? If there are ties, you can list more than 10.

```{r}
top_10 <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(starts_with("ingredient_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("ingredient_"), values_to = "ingredients") %>%
  drop_na(ingredients) %>%
  count(ingredients, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(10)

top_10
```

## 6. Which cocktail(s) has/have the most ingredients?

Count the number of ingredients and filter all the cocktails that has that many.

```{r}
cocktail_data %>%
  select(starts_with("ingredient_")) %>%
  ncol()
colnames(cocktail_data) #also visible in the column names
#there are 6 ingredients max, now If I drop all rows of ingredient_6 that are NA than all that should remain are the 6 ing. cocktails.

sixing_cctls <- cocktail_data %>%
  drop_na(ingredient_6)


```

## 7. How many ingredients appear in only one cocktail (rare ingredient)?

Count all cocktails with only one ingredient, and

```{r}
rare <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(starts_with("ingredient_")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), values_to = "ingredients") %>%
  count(ingredients) %>%
  filter(n == 1) %>%
  pull(ingredients)

length(rare)

```

## 8. Which cocktail has an ingredient that is only used in one cocktail?

```{r}
cocktail_unique <- cocktail_data %>%
  filter(if_any(starts_with("ingredient_"), ~ .x %in% rare)) %>%
  pull(name)
cocktail_unique
```

## 9. What are the cocktails without rare ingredients?

```{r}
cocktail_data %>%
  distinct(name) %>%
  filter(!name %in% cocktail_unique) %>%
  arrange(name) %>%
  pull(name)
```

## 10. Create a cheat sheet for the bartender!

Create a matrix that shows all cocktail names as rows and all ingredients as columns. When a cocktail requires an ingredient, there should be an "X" in the cell, otherwise, the cell should remain empty. Example:

```{r echo=FALSE}
tribble(~name, ~Lime, ~`White rum`, ~`Cane sugar`, ~`Coca-cola`, ~Mint, ~Soda,
        "Caipirissima", "X", "X", "X", "", "", "",
        "Cuba Libre", "X", "X", "", "X","","",
        "Mojito", "X", "X", "", "", "X", "X") %>% 
    relocate(name, sort(names(.)))
```

```{r}
cocktail_data <- cocktail_data[, !duplicated(colnames(cocktail_data))]
colnames(cocktail_data)
cheat_sheet <- cocktail_data %>%
  select(name, starts_with("ingredient_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("ingredient_") , values_to = "ingredients", names_repair = "universal") %>%
  drop_na(ingredients) %>%
  distinct(name...1, ingredients) %>%
  mutate(value= "X" ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ingredients, 
    values_from = value, values_fill = "") %>%
  relocate(name...1, sort(names(.)))




print(cheat_sheet, n = Inf, width = Inf)

```
